## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pull out the drawer of the cabinet with smooth finish and set the small packet of playingcards into it.

Task description: Open the drawer of the smooth wooden cabinet in the center and place the small playing-card pack on the right side of the table inside it.

Success criteria: Put the small packet inside the open drawer, close to its target laterally and longitudinally. Its height must be slightly above its initial tabletop height, within the drawer placement range rather than suspended high above it. The right gripper must be open and release the packet.

## Execution tips

- Only part of the playing-card pack on the right is currently visible. Adjust the view to confirm its full outline and clearance from the neighboring box and bottle before selecting an approach, avoiding grasping the wrong object or sweeping into others.
- Grip a straight section of the horizontal handle away from its end supports, opening slightly wider than its cross-section. Confirm the fingers effectively surround the rod without touching the panel, then pull smoothly outward along the drawer slide direction to reduce slipping and jamming from angled pulling.
- When grasping the small packet, choose straight opposite edges where the pads can make full contact, avoiding thin corners alone. Adjust the opening for packet width and nearby clearance to avoid pushing it toward the table edge during closure.
- Orient the small packet outside the cabinet with enough space so the combined packet-and-finger width fits the drawer opening. Watch the front panel, sidewalls and upper edge to avoid jamming or knocking it down during entry.
- Before releasing, let the small pack be supported by the drawer bottom and leave room for the fingers to open, avoiding a fall during unsupported release or pulling it back out with the gripper.
